source.html

(sentence: “Many were arrested, imprisoned, tortured mercilessly and finally, many were martyred for not recanting their faith.”)
findings.source_quote: Many were arrested, imprisoned, tortured mercilessly and finally, many were martyred for not recanting their faith.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the explicitly religious tone of “martyred” (which carries theological meaning of dying for the faith). Translate with a German word or phrase that retains that nuance, e.g. »schließlich viele als Märtyrer getötet/hingerichtet, weil sie ihren Glauben nicht widerriefen.«
findings.translation_quote: Viele wurden verhaftet, inhaftiert, ohne Erbarmen gefoltert und schließlich hingerichtet, weil sie ihren Glauben nicht widerrufen wollten.

findings.source_quote: In some places, like the Palatinate (Pfaltzland) in Germany, as many as 70% of the inhabitants had died of either war or disease.
findings.suggested_fix: Source uses the form “Pfaltzland” in parentheses. In German the common historical term is “Pfalz” or “Pfalzland”; if you choose to retain the source’s parenthetical spelling, mirror it or else consistently use the contemporary German conventional form. Suggested wording: »… wie in der Pfalz (Pfaltzland) …« or simply »… wie in der Pfalz …«
findings.translation_quote: An manchen Orten, wie in der Pfalz in Deutschland, waren bis zu 70 % der Einwohner entweder durch Krieg oder Krankheit gestorben.

findings.location: source.html paragraph about land patent ("They received a land patent for 10,000 acres")
findings.source_quote: They received a land patent for 10,000 acres for their families and others that might come later.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider localizing the unit name or making it typographically consistent: translate 'acres' to German lower-case (»acres«) or add a parenthetical conversion. Example: »Sie erhielten ein Landpatent über 10.000 Acres (ca. 4.047 ha) …«
findings.translation_quote: Sie erhielten ein Landpatent über 10.000 Acres für ihre Familien und andere, die später kommen könnten.
